correctness.rationale: For n objects and floor(alpha n) attributes with independently missing incidence probability q_n, each formal concept is a maximal independent vertex set of the bipartite missing-incidence graph. Disjoint graph components yield product factors of concept lattices, preserving and reflecting both semidistributivity identities. An exhaustive Prüfer-labelled-tree program classifies every bipartite tree of order at most 7 (total 18,249 labelled across n=1..7); exactly 2,520 labelled 7-paths fail and no smaller tree does; explicit P7 extents witness x∨y=x∨z=top yet x∨(y∧z)=x<top. Independently enumerated all UNLABELLED trees of n=2..7 (1,1,2,3,6,11 types) and found only P7 fails; the two bipartition orientations are dual and have the same both-axes classification. At q=t n^{-7/6}, expected count of P7 copies is q^6/2*((n)_4(m)_3+(n)_3(m)_4)→(alpha³+alpha⁴)t⁶/2; larger components O(n^8 q^7)=O(n^{-1/6}), cycles lower order, and Stein–Chen overlap sum s=1..5 bounds Poisson total variation O(n^{-1/6}). Below scale Markov gives no obstruction; above scale while nq→0, variance/mean²→0 and the proportion of nonisolated paths vanishes, giving loss with high probability. The claimed rate is limited to exact q=t n^{-7/6}; finite tree census is not a probabilistic proof.

value.rationale: Semidistributivity (a key closure-lattice property) in a random formal context is a natural structural event not reducible to the number of concepts. The exact minimal seven-vertex missing-incidence path obstruction, Poisson limiting probability and nontrivial scale n^{-7/6} identify the first sparse-loss transition in a full fixed-aspect random-context family. It is a motivated sharp asymptotic/forbidden-substructure theorem rather than an arbitrary small-parameter census.
